narrative.overview:
The timetable behaves like something iOS would ship: a black ground, greys that rise in lightness as surfaces come forward, one blue that means "now / today / you are here", and system type set tight and confident. The page is read in a hurry, on a phone, between buildings, so every surface answers what, when, where before it says anything about itself.

Density is calm rather than sparse. On phones each day is an inset grouped list; on desktop the same rows become tiles placed in a true day × block grid, so the whole week sits in one viewport. The memorable move is the subject capsule: a 4px colour bar that names the subject and, for the class in progress, fills top to bottom as the class elapses, in the rows and in the Live card at the top.

Motion is physical and short: expo-out arrivals, springs on press and on the floating pill, View Transitions that slide the week sideways in the direction you moved, a bottom sheet that rides the iOS sheet curve. Movement is reserved for state changes; nothing loops except the live dot of the class that is on now.
keyCharacteristics: Pure black ground; depth from surface lightness and a 6% top edge-light, not drop shadows.
One accent, used for now, today, focus and selection only.
System SF / Inter, sentence case, tabular numerals; no monospace, no all-caps labels.
Subject colour lives only in the capsule and legend dots.
Frosted glass only where something floats over content: the stuck week bar and the "Bieżący tydzień" pill.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue means "now, today, or focused" and nothing else. Never use it for decoration, headings or inactive states.

rules.name: The Capsule Rule
rules.body: Subject colour appears only as the 4px capsule and the 10px legend dot. Never tint text, card backgrounds or borders with a subject colour.

rules.name: The Receding Past Rule
rules.body: Past days and finished classes step down one text token (label → secondary, secondary → tertiary) and dim their capsule to 45%. They never drop below label-tertiary, so they stay AA-legible.

rules.name: The Tabular Time Rule
rules.body: Every time, date, count and room is set with tabular numerals so columns of times align.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase labels or eyebrows anywhere; status lines read as sentences ("Następne · za 25 min").

rules.name: The No-Glow Rule
rules.body: No coloured or zero-offset halo shadows. State is shown with a 1px accent ring and a tinted fill, never a glow.

rules.name: The Glass-Only-When-Floating Rule
rules.body: Backdrop blur is allowed only on elements that sit over scrolling content. It is off while the bar rests in place.

dos: Do keep the ground pure #000 and lift surfaces only through the surface-* ramp plus edge-light.
Do use the accent only for now, today, focus and selection (The One Blue Rule).

Do animate transform and opacity: 150ms feedback, 300ms state, 420–520ms transitions and sheets, expo-out (cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1)) for arrivals, cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1) for the sheet, springs for press and the floating pill.
Do give every motion a reduced-motion path that keeps fades and drops travel.
Do keep all styling in hashed <style> blocks and set dynamic values with CSSOM custom properties; the CSP blocks inline style attributes.
donts: Don't add coloured glows, gradient text, side stripes on card edges, or emoji or glyph icons.
Don't use uppercase eyebrows or labels above headings, or a monospace face for data.
Don't put backdrop blur on anything that does not float over content, or loop an animation on anything that is not live.
Don't tint text or surfaces with subject colours (The Capsule Rule).
Don't add WAT logos, crests or official-looking wording; the site is an unofficial student view.
